doc.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11

title: Tony Giardina's band at Millenburg, and Fay and Gahagan
summary: Personnel of Frank Christian's band and Millenburg's rival dance halls run by Fay and Gahagan.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I wish I could see that picture of Tony Giardino. He was in a similar band I think at one time.
Well Tony Giardino was with his brothers. He was playing most of the time. He was playing with Frank.
Because I used to come to town and I'd go out to Millenburg and uh see him playing out there.

Because they had uh there was Frank, my brother Charlie, Tony Giardino, Chink Martin, uh Tots on drums, uh Willie guitar on bass. Willie guitar on bass. And I think he had a violin. Susu's cripple fella. Uh uh yeah uh Susu? Uh uh no uh the tailor uh Raymond? He tell me he just died. No uh.
Joe uh I don't know. He lived right right by Washington Square on Royal and Lesion Field there.
I know all right I'll figure it out.
We'll find out. But if his uh uh Joe Palizzi. Palizzi? Joe Palizzi.
I thought he was a clarinet player.
Well Joe he used to play a little clarinet but he used to play violin. Joe Palizzi.
He tell me he died. Those days in uh Millenburg at the very beginning his brother would play in the center which was called Corellas.
And we would be playing on the very end for a place called Fay and Gahagan. Johnny Fay I guess he's one of the biggest politicians in town. He was last time I think unless he's dead I don't know.
Rick of Ford and Fay. I mean he's a very big man. They died for it. And we had. Rick of Ford was in a lot of stuff. Well Rick of Ford and Fay was uh you know big men.
They used to have a dancing school right on.
Because Gahagan died. He was a good politician. One late. And uh we would be playing on the end of the wharf and uh both places would do good business because we both had good bands.
